blocks.original_text:
- name: int_pendo__conversion_funnel_analysis
      description: Daily account+app funnel metrics from Pendo events with 30-day rolling averages, trend, health rating, and optimization recommendations
      grain: One row per account_id, app_id, event_date
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_pendo__event
      - staging.stg_pendo__feature_event
      - staging.stg_pendo__page_event
      business_logic: 'Build daily account-level conversion funnel metrics and 30-day cohort summaries: - daily_events (union all) - Page views: from staging.stg_pendo__event as event_type=page_view; fields include visitor_id, account_id, app_id, event_date (day-level from occurred_at), entity_id=page_id, num_events, num_minutes. - Feature interactions: from staging.stg_pendo__feature_event as event_type=feature_click; entity_id=feature_id; carry num_events and num_minutes. - Deep page interactions: from staging.stg_pendo__page_event as event_type=page_interaction; per visitor/account/app/day/page aggregate counts of interactions (num_events) and summed minutes (num_minutes). - user_daily_funnel (per visitor_id, account_id, app_id, event_date) - Presence flags by type: has_page_view, has_feature_interaction, has_deep_interaction set to 1 if any such event exists that day, else 0. - Distinct entities: unique_pages_viewed, unique_features_used, unique_pages_interacted are distinct counts of entity_id by type. - Totals: total_page_events/total_feature_events/total_interaction_events and corresponding minutes are summed by type. - funnel_progression (per visitor/day) - Funnel stage precedence: Deep Engaged (all three flags=1) > Feature User (page and feature flags=1) > Page Visitor (page flag=1) > No Activity. - engagement_score = 0.1×total_page_events + 0.3×total_feature_events + 0.6×total_interaction_events + 0.05×(total_page_minutes + total_feature_minutes + total_interaction_minutes). - session_quality: High Quality if total_minutes≥10 and unique_pages_viewed≥3 and unique_features_used≥2; else Medium Quality if total_minutes≥5 and unique_pages_viewed≥2; else Low Quality if total_page_minutes≥1; else Bounce. Here total_minutes = total_page_minutes + total_feature_minutes + total_interaction_minutes. - account_funnel_metrics (per account_id, app_id, event_date) - Visitor counts: total_visitors = distinct visitor_id; visitors_with_page_views/features/deep = distinct visitors with the corresponding presence flag=1. - Conversion rates: page_to_feature = visitors_with_feature_use / visitors_with_page_views; feature_to_deep = visitors_with_deep_engagement / visitors_with_feature_use; overall = visitors_with_deep_engagement / visitors_with_page_views. If the denominator is 0, the rate is NULL. - Averages: avg_engagement_score and avg_pages_per_visitor are averaged over visitors with has_page_view=1; avg_features_per_user over visitors with has_feature_interaction=1; if no qualifying visitors, result is NULL. - Quality rates: high_quality_session_rate = distinct visitors with session_quality=''High Quality'' divided by total_visitors; bounce_rate = distinct visitors with session_quality=''Bounce'' divided by total_visitors; NULL if total_visitors=0. - conversion_cohort_analysis (per account_id, app_id; joined back to each daily row) - 30-day rolling averages relative to today (lower bound inclusive): average of daily page_to_feature, feature_to_deep, and overall conversion rates for dates on or after 30 days before today. - conversion_rate_trend = average overall conversion rate for dates on or after 7 days before today minus the average for dates from 30 to 7 days before today; both windows include the day 7 days ago. - funnel_health_rating by the 30-day average overall rate: Excellent (≥0.3), Good (≥0.2), Fair (≥0.1), else Poor. If the 30-day average is NULL, rating is Poor. - optimization_recommendation (first matching rule): if the 30-day average page→feature rate < 0.2 then “Focus on feature discovery and onboarding”; else if the 30-day average feature→deep rate < 0.3 then “Improve feature engagement and user guidance”; else if the 30-day average bounce rate > 0.6 then “Reduce bounce rate through better landing experience”; else “Maintain current optimization efforts”. - Final step: left join the cohort metrics to the daily account_funnel_metrics by account_id and app_id; set calculated_at to the query execution timestamp. Distinct counting ensures a visitor is counted once per day; averages ignore NULLs; no rounding is applied.'
      columns:
      - name: account_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Account identifier; grouping key for metrics and cohort join
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: app_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Application identifier within the account; grouping key for metrics and cohort join
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: event_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Day-level calendar date derived from occurred_at used for daily aggregation
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: total_visitors
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct visitor_id count per account_id, app_id, event_date across all event types
      - name: visitors_with_page_views
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct visitors with has_page_view=1 (at least one page_view event on the date)
      - name: visitors_with_feature_use
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct visitors with has_feature_interaction=1 (at least one feature_click event on the date)
      - name: visitors_with_deep_engagement
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct visitors with has_deep_interaction=1 (at least one page_interaction event on the date)
      - name: page_to_feature_conversion_rate
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: visitors_with_feature_use divided by visitors_with_page_views; NULL if visitors_with_page_views=0
      - name: feature_to_deep_conversion_rate
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: visitors_with_deep_engagement divided by visitors_with_feature_use; NULL if visitors_with_feature_use=0
      - name: overall_conversion_rate
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: visitors_with_deep_engagement divided by visitors_with_page_views; NULL if visitors_with_page_views=0
      - name: avg_engagement_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average engagement_score over visitors with has_page_view=1; NULL if none
      - name: avg_pages_per_visitor
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average unique_pages_viewed over visitors with has_page_view=1; NULL if none
      - name: avg_features_per_user
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average unique_features_used over visitors with has_feature_interaction=1; NULL if none
      - name: high_quality_session_rate
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: Distinct visitors with session_quality='High Quality' divided by total_visitors; NULL if total_visitors=0
      - name: bounce_rate
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: Distinct visitors with session_quality='Bounce' divided by total_visitors; NULL if total_visitors=0
      - name: avg_30d_page_to_feature_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of daily page_to_feature_conversion_rate for dates on or after 30 days before today (inclusive); NULL if no data
      - name: avg_30d_feature_to_deep_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of daily feature_to_deep_conversion_rate for dates on or after 30 days before today (inclusive); NULL if no data
      - name: avg_30d_overall_conversion_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average of daily overall_conversion_rate for dates on or after 30 days before today (inclusive); NULL if no data
      - name: conversion_rate_trend
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Avg over dates on/after 7 days before today minus avg over dates from 30 to 7 days before today; both include the 7-days-ago date; NULL if either window lacks data
      - name: funnel_health_rating
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Rating by 30-day average overall rate: Excellent (≥0.3), Good (≥0.2), Fair (≥0.1), else Poor'
      - name: optimization_recommendation
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Based on 30-day averages: feature discovery if page→feature<0.2; engagement if feature→deep<0.3; reduce bounce if bounce rate>0.6; else maintain'
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Timestamp of computation set to the query execution time

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_pendo__customer_rfm_analysis
      description: Visitor–account level RFM segmentation with strategies and account-level health metrics
      grain: One row per visitor_id + account_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_pendo__event
      - intermediate.int_pendo__latest_visitor_account
      business_logic: '1) Aggregate events by visitor_id + account_id: - Active days: number of distinct calendar days with any event (based on occurred_at). - Active months: number of distinct calendar months with any event. - Total usage: sum of num_events and sum of num_minutes. - Average per record: mean of num_events (also compute mean of num_minutes for internal use). - Event records: number of event rows contributing to the group. - First/last activity dates: earliest and latest calendar day with any event. 2) For each visitor, count distinct associated accounts from the latest mapping; if missing, default the count to 1. 3) Keep only visitor–account pairs with at least one event. Compute: - recency_days: days from the last activity date to today. - customer_lifetime_days: days from the first activity date to today. 4) RFM scoring (1–5): - recency_score: 5 (≤7 days), 4 (≤30), 3 (≤90), 2 (≤180), else 1. - frequency_score from active days: 5 (≥50), 4 (≥25), 3 (≥10), 2 (≥5), else 1. - magnitude_score from total events and total minutes: 5 (≥1000 and ≥500), 4 (≥500 and ≥200), 3 (≥200 and ≥100), 2 (≥50 and ≥30), else 1. 5) Derive segment and value metrics: - rfm_composite_score: 0.3*recency + 0.4*frequency + 0.3*magnitude (stored with one decimal). - rfm_segment (first matching rule wins): • Champions: recency ≥4 and frequency ≥4 and magnitude ≥4 • Loyal Customers: frequency ≥4 and magnitude ≥4 • Potential Loyalists: recency ≥4 and frequency ≥3 and magnitude ≤3 • New Customers: recency ≥4 and frequency ≤2 and lifetime ≤60 days • Promising: magnitude ≥4 and frequency ≤3 • Customers Needing Attention: recency ≤2 and frequency ≥3 and magnitude ≥3 • About to Sleep: recency = 3 and frequency ≤3 and magnitude ≤3 • At Risk: recency ≤2 and frequency ≤2 and magnitude ≤3 • Cannot Be Retrieved: recency = 1 and frequency ≤2 • Hibernating: recency ≤2 and magnitude ≥4 • Others: otherwise - customer_value_tier from the product of the three scores: High Value (≥60), Medium Value (≥24), Low Value (≥8), else Minimal Value. - recommended_strategy: fixed text per rfm_segment. - predicted_clv_tier: based on rfm_segment; Very High CLV only for Champions or Loyal Customers with lifetime >180 days. - action_priority: fixed text per rfm_segment. 6) Account-level aggregation (per account across all visitor rows): - total_visitors. - Segment counts: Champions, Loyal Customers, Potential Loyalists, New Customers, and At Risk (At Risk + Cannot Be Retrieved). - Ratios (floating-point): • high_value_ratio = number of High Value visitors divided by total_visitors, • top_segment_ratio = number of Champions or Loyal Customers divided by total_visitors, • at_risk_ratio = number of At Risk or Cannot Be Retrieved divided by total_visitors. - Averages: mean composite score and means of the three scores. 7) Final output: - Left join account metrics to each visitor–account row. - calculated_at = the query execution timestamp. - Grain: one row per visitor_id + account_id.'
      columns:
      - name: visitor_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Visitor identifier paired with account_id; non-null key.
      - name: account_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Account identifier paired with visitor_id; used to attach account metrics.
      - name: recency_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Days since the most recent activity date to today.
      - name: count_active_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct calendar days with at least one event; duplicates within a day counted once.
      - name: count_active_months
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct calendar months with at least one event; duplicates within a month counted once.
      - name: total_events
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of num_events for the visitor–account; only pairs with at least one event are included.
      - name: total_minutes
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of num_minutes for the visitor–account; non-null as only event-bearing pairs are included.
      - name: average_daily_events
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Mean of num_events across event records for the visitor–account; no rounding.
      - name: count_associated_accounts
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct accounts linked to the visitor from the latest mapping; defaults to 1 when missing.
      - name: customer_lifetime_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Days from the first activity date to today.
      - name: recency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Recency score (1–5): 5 if ≤7 days, 4 if ≤30, 3 if ≤90, 2 if ≤180, else 1.'
      - name: frequency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Frequency score (1–5) from active days: 5 if ≥50, 4 if ≥25, 3 if ≥10, 2 if ≥5, else 1.'
      - name: magnitude_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Magnitude score (1–5) from total events and minutes: 5 if ≥1000 and ≥500; 4 if ≥500 and ≥200; 3 if ≥200 and ≥100; 2 if ≥50 and ≥30; else 1.'
      - name: rfm_composite_score
        data_type: DECIMAL(14,1)
        description: Weighted sum 0.3*recency + 0.4*frequency + 0.3*magnitude stored with one decimal.
      - name: rfm_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Segment assigned by ordered rules using the three scores and lifetime; first matching rule applies.
      - name: customer_value_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Tier from the product of the three scores: High (≥60), Medium (≥24), Low (≥8), else Minimal.'
      - name: recommended_strategy
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Deterministic recommendation text mapped from rfm_segment; default is Standard engagement tactics.
      - name: predicted_clv_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: CLV tier from rfm_segment; Very High requires Champions or Loyal Customers with lifetime >180 days.
      - name: action_priority
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Next-step priority mapped from rfm_segment: Retention & Advocacy, Growth & Upsell, Onboarding & Education, Re-engagement, Win-back or Deprioritize, Reactivation, or Monitor.'
      - name: account_total_visitors
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of visitor rows for the account; denominator for the ratios.
      - name: account_high_value_ratio
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: Share of High Value visitors over total_visitors using floating-point division.
      - name: account_top_segment_ratio
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: Share of Champions or Loyal Customers over total_visitors using floating-point division.
      - name: account_at_risk_ratio
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: Share of At Risk or Cannot Be Retrieved visitors over total_visitors using floating-point division.
      - name: account_avg_rfm_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Mean rfm_composite_score across all visitors in the account.
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Execution timestamp applied uniformly to all output rows.

columns.name: frequency_score

columns.name: magnitude_score

columns.name: rfm_segment

columns.name: customer_value_tier

columns.name: action_priority

columns.name: account_top_segment_ratio
columns.description: Share of Champions or Loyal Customers over total_visitors using floating-point division.

columns.name: account_at_risk_ratio
columns.description: Share of At Risk or Cannot Be Retrieved visitors over total_visitors using floating-point division.

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_pendo__data_quality_checks
      description: Consolidated data quality report across Pendo staging tables (summary, per-table completeness, consistency issues, and business logic violations)
      grain: 'One row per report line: 1 summary row; per-table rows for completeness; per-check-type rows for consistency; per-violation-type rows for business logic'
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_pendo__account_history
      - staging.stg_pendo__visitor_history
      - staging.stg_pendo__event
      business_logic: 'Build a four-section report by computing intermediate checks and then UNION ALLing section-specific rows (column meanings vary by section; see column rules below). No output ordering is enforced. All timestamps use current_timestamp at query time. 1) Data completeness checks: - account_history: total records; count of NULL account_id; count of NULL first_visit_at; count of NULL last_visit_at; other counts set to 0. - visitor_history: total records; count of NULL visitor_id; other counts set to 0; sixth position is count of NULL account_id. - event: total records; second–sixth positions respectively count NULL visitor_id, NULL account_id, NULL occurred_at, NULL app_id, and count of num_events that are NULL or negative. - Later UNIONs align values by position from the first select’s column order. 2) Data consistency checks: five issue types with counts and descriptions: - timestamp_consistency: events with occurred_at in the future. - account_visitor_relationship: visitor_history rows whose non-NULL account_id does not exist in account_history. - event_visitor_relationship: events whose visitor_id does not exist in visitor_history. - negative_metrics: events with negative num_minutes or num_events. - chronological_consistency: accounts where first_visit_at and last_visit_at are both present and first_visit_at is after last_visit_at. 3) Business logic violations: four rules with counts and descriptions: - impossible_session_duration: events with num_minutes > 480. - excessive_daily_events: per visitor and day, sum num_events; count groups with sum > 10000. - duplicate_primary_keys: difference between total events and distinct event_key. - inactive_paying_accounts: accounts with no events in the last 90 days. 4) Summary quality metrics: - completeness_score: compute the share of complete records by subtracting the ratio of (sum of NULL primary keys + sum of missing names + sum of missing first visits) to (three times the sum of total records) from 1, then multiply by 100; return NULL if the denominator is zero. - consistency_score: compute 1 minus the ratio of total consistency violations to the overall total records, then multiply by 100; return NULL if the denominator is zero. - business_logic_score: compute 1 minus the ratio of total business logic violations to the overall total records, then multiply by 100; return NULL if the denominator is zero. - These totals are evaluated over a Cartesian product of the completeness, consistency, and business-logic CTEs, so each component’s sum is multiplied by the row counts of the other two CTEs. - calculated_at uses the current time. 5) Final UNION ALL report rows: - Data Quality Summary: 1 row with the three percentage scores; overall_quality_score is their average; quality_grade is Excellent (>=95), Good (>=85), Fair (>=70), else Poor; calculated_at from the summary CTE. - Data Completeness Details: one row per table_name with column mapping by position: table_name (text), total_records, null_primary_keys, missing_names, missing_first_visit (as text), and calculated_at as current time. - Data Consistency Issues: one row per check_type with column mapping by position: check_type (text), total_violations, NULL, NULL, violation_description (text), and calculated_at as current time. - Business Logic Violations: one row per violation_type with column mapping by position: violation_type (text), violation_count, NULL, NULL, description (text), and calculated_at as current time. Notes: - Outlier detection and data freshness CTEs are computed but not included in the final UNION, so they do not appear in the output. - DuckDB coerces types across the UNION by position: columns 2 and 6 are VARCHAR; columns 3–5 are FLOAT; NULLs are preserved.'
      columns:
      - name: report_section
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Section label; one of 'Data Quality Summary', 'Data Completeness Details', 'Data Consistency Issues', 'Business Logic Violations'
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: completeness_score
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Section-dependent text: summary shows the completeness percentage as text (no explicit rounding); completeness details show table_name; consistency issues show check_type; business logic violations show violation_type; summary can be NULL if the denominator is zero.'
      - name: consistency_score
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: 'Numeric metric by section: summary shows the consistency percentage; completeness details show total_records; consistency issues show total_violations; business logic violations show violation_count.'
      - name: business_logic_score
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: 'Numeric metric by section: summary shows the business logic percentage; completeness details show null_primary_keys; consistency issues and business logic violations are NULL.'
      - name: overall_quality_score
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: 'Numeric metric by section: summary is the average of the three percentage scores; completeness details show missing_names; consistency issues and business logic violations are NULL.'
      - name: quality_grade
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Section-dependent text: summary grade (Excellent/Good/Fair/Poor using thresholds 95/85/70); completeness details show missing_first_visit as text; consistency issues show violation_description; business logic violations show description.'
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Timestamp when the row was computed; summary uses its CTE value; other sections use current query time.
        tests:
        - not_null

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_pendo__product_health_metrics
      description: Overall product health metrics combining NPS, feature adoption, retention, and engagement with derived grades and risk
      grain: One row per account_id and fam.app_id; if no feature_adoption_metrics row exists, rows appear per account_id with app_id NULL (there can be multiple such rows per account when only engagement data exists)
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_pendo__latest_nps_rating
      - staging.stg_pendo__feature_event
      - staging.stg_pendo__event
      business_logic: '- NPS metrics (by account_id from intermediate.int_pendo__latest_nps_rating): - total_nps_responses is the total row count per account; avg_nps_score is the mean of nps_rating (ignoring NULLs). - promoter_rate is the share of rows with nps_rating ≥ 9 using total_nps_responses as the denominator (NULL ratings not counted in the numerator but included in the denominator). - detractor_rate is the share of rows with nps_rating ≤ 6 using total_nps_responses as the denominator (NULL ratings not counted in the numerator but included in the denominator). - net_promoter_score = promoter_rate − detractor_rate. - Feature adoption metrics (by app_id, account_id from staging.stg_pendo__feature_event): - total_features_available is distinct features; features_used is distinct features with any usage (>0 events); features_heavily_used is distinct features with ≥10 events. - total_users is distinct visitors; active_feature_users is distinct visitors with any feature usage (>0 events). - feature_adoption_rate = features_used ÷ total_features_available (returns NULL when total_features_available = 0). - feature_depth_adoption_rate = features_heavily_used ÷ total_features_available (returns NULL when total_features_available = 0). - user_feature_adoption_rate = active_feature_users ÷ total_users (returns NULL when total_users = 0). - avg_features_per_user = features_used ÷ active_feature_users (returns NULL when active_feature_users = 0). - Distinct counts exclude NULL IDs; duplicates are removed. - Visitor aggregated metrics (by account_id, visitor_id from staging.stg_pendo__event): - count_active_days is the distinct count of active calendar days; sum_events and sum_minutes are totals across events; last_event_on is the most recent active calendar day. - User retention metrics (by account_id from visitor_aggregated_metrics): - total_users is distinct visitors. - retention_7d/30d/90d are the shares of visitors whose last_event_on is within 7/30/90 days of current_date; denominators are total_users (no explicit zero-division guard). - highly_active_user_rate is the share of visitors with count_active_days ≥ 20 (denominator is total_users; no explicit zero-division guard). - avg_lifetime_events is the mean of sum_events per visitor; avg_active_days_per_user is the mean of count_active_days per visitor. - Engagement quality metrics (by account_id, app_id from staging.stg_pendo__event): - avg_session_duration is the mean minutes per session; avg_events_per_session is the mean events per session (NULLs ignored in averages). - unique_users is distinct visitors; total_sessions is the session row count; sessions_per_user = total_sessions ÷ unique_users (no explicit zero-division guard). - deep_engagement_session_rate is the share of sessions with ≥10 minutes or ≥20 events (denominator is total_sessions). - power_user_rate assumes 20% are high-frequency users: equals 0.2 when unique_users > 0, else NULL. - Product health scores: - Join feature_adoption_metrics (fam) and user_retention_metrics (urm) with a full outer join on account_id. - Join engagement_quality_metrics (eqm) with a full outer join on the coalesced account_id from fam/urm and require app_id to match fam.app_id; rows with only engagement data are kept but will have app_id NULL in the output. - Join nps_metrics (nm) with a left join on the coalesced account_id from fam/urm; NPS does not attach for engagement-only rows. - account_id is coalesced from fam, then urm, then eqm; app_id comes only from fam. - overall_health_score is a 0–100 score capped at 100, computed as the sum of: - up to 25 points from NPS by scaling net_promoter_score from [-1,1] to [0,25] (missing treated as 0), - up to 25 points from feature_adoption_rate (missing treated as 0), - up to 25 points from retention_30d (missing treated as 0), - up to 25 points from engagement: deep_engagement_session_rate (up to 12.5) and power_user_rate (up to 12.5) (missing treated as 0). - Health categorization: - health_grade: Excellent (score ≥ 80), Good (≥ 60), Fair (≥ 40), Poor (≥ 20), else Critical. - primary_improvement_area (first match wins): if net_promoter_score is missing treat as −1; if feature_adoption_rate, retention_30d, or deep_engagement_session_rate are missing treat as 0; then check in order: NPS < 0, adoption < 0.3, 30‑day retention < 0.5, deep engagement < 0.2; otherwise maintain/optimize. - risk_level: High Risk if score < 30; Medium Risk if (score < 50 and 30‑day retention < 0.4, treating missing retention as 0) or net_promoter_score < −0.2 (treating missing NPS as 0); else Low. - calculated_at is set to the current timestamp at execution.'
      columns:
      - name: account_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Account identifier coalesced from feature adoption, retention, or engagement sources; always populated
      - name: app_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Application identifier taken from feature adoption metrics; NULL when no feature adoption row exists (possible multiple NULL-app rows per account from engagement-only data)
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Execution timestamp set via current_timestamp (database time zone)
      - name: overall_health_score
        data_type: FLOAT

      - name: user_feature_adoption_rate

        description: Proportion of visitors who used any feature over all distinct visitors; returns NULL when no visitors
      - name: retention_7d

        description: Share of visitors whose last active day is within 7 days of current_date; denominator is distinct visitors and no zero-division guard is applied
      - name: retention_30d

        description: Share of visitors whose last active day is within 30 days of current_date; denominator is distinct visitors and no zero-division guard is applied
      - name: retention_90d

      - name: avg_events_per_session

      - name: total_features_available

      - name: power_user_rate

      - name: highly_active_user_rate

specification.name: int_pendo__product_health_metrics
specification.description: Overall product health metrics combining NPS, feature adoption, retention, and engagement with derived grades and risk
specification.grain: One row per account_id and fam.app_id; if no feature_adoption_metrics row exists, rows appear per account_id with app_id NULL (there can be multiple such rows per account when only engagement data exists)
specification.business_logic: - NPS metrics (by account_id from intermediate.int_pendo__latest_nps_rating): - total_nps_responses is the total row count per account; avg_nps_score is the mean of nps_rating (ignoring NULLs). - promoter_rate is the share of rows with nps_rating ≥ 9 using total_nps_responses as the denominator (NULL ratings not counted in the numerator but included in the denominator). - detractor_rate is the share of rows with nps_rating ≤ 6 using total_nps_responses as the denominator (NULL ratings not counted in the numerator but included in the denominator). - net_promoter_score = promoter_rate − detractor_rate. - Feature adoption metrics (by app_id, account_id from staging.stg_pendo__feature_event): - total_features_available is distinct features; features_used is distinct features with any usage (>0 events); features_heavily_used is distinct features with ≥10 events. - total_users is distinct visitors; active_feature_users is distinct visitors with any feature usage (>0 events). - feature_adoption_rate = features_used ÷ total_features_available (returns NULL when total_features_available = 0). - feature_depth_adoption_rate = features_heavily_used ÷ total_features_available (returns NULL when total_features_available = 0). - user_feature_adoption_rate = active_feature_users ÷ total_users (returns NULL when total_users = 0). - avg_features_per_user = features_used ÷ active_feature_users (returns NULL when active_feature_users = 0). - Distinct counts exclude NULL IDs; duplicates are removed. - Visitor aggregated metrics (by account_id, visitor_id from staging.stg_pendo__event): - count_active_days is the distinct count of active calendar days; sum_events and sum_minutes are totals across events; last_event_on is the most recent active calendar day. - User retention metrics (by account_id from visitor_aggregated_metrics): - total_users is distinct visitors. - retention_7d/30d/90d are the shares of visitors whose last_event_on is within 7/30/90 days of current_date; denominators are total_users (no explicit zero-division guard). - highly_active_user_rate is the share of visitors with count_active_days ≥ 20 (denominator is total_users; no explicit zero-division guard). - avg_lifetime_events is the mean of sum_events per visitor; avg_active_days_per_user is the mean of count_active_days per visitor. - Engagement quality metrics (by account_id, app_id from staging.stg_pendo__event): - avg_session_duration is the mean minutes per session; avg_events_per_session is the mean events per session (NULLs ignored in averages). - unique_users is distinct visitors; total_sessions is the session row count; sessions_per_user = total_sessions ÷ unique_users (no explicit zero-division guard). - deep_engagement_session_rate is the share of sessions with ≥10 minutes or ≥20 events (denominator is total_sessions). - power_user_rate assumes 20% are high-frequency users: equals 0.2 when unique_users > 0, else NULL. - Product health scores: - Join feature_adoption_metrics (fam) and user_retention_metrics (urm) with a full outer join on account_id. - Join engagement_quality_metrics (eqm) with a full outer join on the coalesced account_id from fam/urm and require app_id to match fam.app_id; rows with only engagement data are kept but will have app_id NULL in the output. - Join nps_metrics (nm) with a left join on the coalesced account_id from fam/urm; NPS does not attach for engagement-only rows. - account_id is coalesced from fam, then urm, then eqm; app_id comes only from fam. - overall_health_score is a 0–100 score capped at 100, computed as the sum of: - up to 25 points from NPS by scaling net_promoter_score from [-1,1] to [0,25] (missing treated as 0), - up to 25 points from feature_adoption_rate (missing treated as 0), - up to 25 points from retention_30d (missing treated as 0), - up to 25 points from engagement: deep_engagement_session_rate (up to 12.5) and power_user_rate (up to 12.5) (missing treated as 0). - Health categorization: - health_grade: Excellent (score ≥ 80), Good (≥ 60), Fair (≥ 40), Poor (≥ 20), else Critical. - primary_improvement_area (first match wins): if net_promoter_score is missing treat as −1; if feature_adoption_rate, retention_30d, or deep_engagement_session_rate are missing treat as 0; then check in order: NPS < 0, adoption < 0.3, 30‑day retention < 0.5, deep engagement < 0.2; otherwise maintain/optimize. - risk_level: High Risk if score < 30; Medium Risk if (score < 50 and 30‑day retention < 0.4, treating missing retention as 0) or net_promoter_score < −0.2 (treating missing NPS as 0); else Low. - calculated_at is set to the current timestamp at execution.

cte_definitions.sql: SELECT *, CASE WHEN user_age_days <= 30 AND count_active_days <= 7 THEN 'New User' WHEN user_age_days BETWEEN 30 AND 90 AND activity_density > 0.2 AND days_since_last_active <= 30 THEN 'Growing User' WHEN user_age_days > 90 AND activity_density > 0.1 AND days_since_last_active <= 60 AND usage_intensity IN ('Medium', 'High') THEN 'Mature User' WHEN activity_density > 0.3 AND usage_intensity = 'High' AND days_since_last_active <= 14 THEN 'Power User' WHEN user_age_days > 30 AND days_since_last_active BETWEEN 30 AND 90 AND count_active_days >= 3 THEN 'At Risk' WHEN days_since_last_active > 90 THEN 'Churned' ELSE 'Dormant' END AS lifecycle_stage, LEAST(100, activity_density * 30 + CASE usage_intensity WHEN 'High' THEN 25 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 15 WHEN 'Low' THEN 8 ELSE 2 END + CASE WHEN days_since_last_active <= 7 THEN 25 WHEN days_since_last_active <= 30 THEN 15 WHEN days_since_last_active <= 90 THEN 5 ELSE 0 END + LEAST(20, count_active_months * 2)) AS user_value_score, CASE WHEN days_since_last_active <= 30 AND user_age_days > 60 THEN CASE WHEN activity_density > 0.5 THEN 'Increasing' WHEN activity_density > 0.2 THEN 'Stable' ELSE 'Declining' END WHEN days_since_last_active <= 30 THEN 'New/Recent' ELSE 'Inactive' END AS engagement_trend FROM b

      business_logic: '- Aggregate events by (visitor_id, account_id): - count_active_days: number of distinct calendar days with at least one event. - count_active_months: number of distinct calendar months with at least one event. - sum_events: total of num_events; NULLs are ignored and NULL is returned only if all values are NULL. - sum_minutes: total of num_minutes; NULLs are ignored and NULL is returned only if all values are NULL. - average_daily_events: arithmetic mean of num_events across grouped rows with values. - average_daily_minutes: arithmetic mean of num_minutes across grouped rows with values. - first_event_on: earliest event date (calendar day). - last_event_on: most recent event date (calendar day). - Keep only groups where first_event_on is present. - Derive: - user_age_days: whole days between first_event_on and today. - days_since_last_active: whole days between last_event_on and today. - activity_density: if user_age_days > 0, count_active_days divided by user_age_days; otherwise 0. - usage_intensity: label by average_daily_events thresholds: High (≥50), Medium (≥20), Low (≥5), Minimal (<5). - Classify lifecycle_stage in this order (first match wins): 1) New User: user_age_days ≤ 30 and count_active_days ≤ 7. 2) Growing User: user_age_days between 30 and 90, activity_density > 0.2, and days_since_last_active ≤ 30. 3) Mature User: user_age_days > 90, activity_density > 0.1, days_since_last_active ≤ 60, and usage_intensity is Medium or High. 4) Power User: activity_density > 0.3, usage_intensity is High, and days_since_last_active ≤ 14. 5) At Risk: user_age_days > 30, days_since_last_active between 30 and 90, and count_active_days ≥ 3. 6) Churned: days_since_last_active > 90. 7) Otherwise: Dormant. - Compute user_value_score and cap at 100: - activity_density × 30 - plus intensity points: High=25, Medium=15, Low=8, Minimal=2 - plus recency points: ≤7 days=25, ≤30 days=15, ≤90 days=5, else 0 - plus min(20, count_active_months × 2). - Determine engagement_trend (first match wins): - If days_since_last_active ≤ 30 and user_age_days > 60: Increasing if activity_density > 0.5; Stable if > 0.2; otherwise Declining. - Else if days_since_last_active ≤ 30: New/Recent. - Else: Inactive. - Determine churn_risk_level (first match wins): - If lifecycle_stage is Churned: Already Churned. - Else if lifecycle_stage is At Risk: High Risk. - Else Medium Risk if (days_since_last_active > 30 and usage_intensity is Minimal or Low) or (activity_density < 0.1 and user_age_days > 90); otherwise Low Risk. - Flags: - is_valuable_user: true for Power User or Mature User; else false. - needs_attention: true for At Risk or Churned; else false. - is_new_user: true for New User; else false. - calculated_at is set to the query execution timestamp.'
      columns:

        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Visitor identifier; metrics are aggregated per account, so a visitor may appear in multiple rows across accounts
      - name: first_event_on

      - name: last_event_on

      - name: days_since_last_active
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Whole days from last_event_on to current_date; non-negative
      - name: count_active_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct calendar days with at least one event
      - name: count_active_months
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct calendar months with at least one event
      - name: sum_events
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Total of num_events across grouped records; ignores NULLs; NULL only if all inputs are NULL
      - name: sum_minutes
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Total of num_minutes across grouped records; ignores NULLs; NULL only if all inputs are NULL
      - name: average_daily_events
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Mean of num_events across grouped records with values; no rounding
      - name: average_daily_minutes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Mean of num_minutes across grouped records with values; no rounding
      - name: activity_density
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: If user_age_days > 0, count_active_days divided by user_age_days; otherwise 0; no rounding
      - name: usage_intensity
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Label based on average_daily_events: High (≥50), Medium (≥20), Low (≥5), else Minimal'
      - name: lifecycle_stage
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Lifecycle label from the ordered rules in business_logic; first match wins
      - name: user_value_score
        data_type: FLOAT
        description: Composite score capped at 100 from activity density, intensity points, recency points, and active months; no rounding
      - name: engagement_trend
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Trend based on recency and activity density: Increasing/Stable/Declining when recently active and age > 60, else New/Recent if recently active, else Inactive'
      - name: churn_risk_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Risk label: Already Churned for Churned stage; High Risk for At Risk stage; otherwise Medium Risk per recency/intensity or low density with age > 90; else Low Risk'
      - name: is_valuable_user
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: True if lifecycle_stage is Power User or Mature User; otherwise false
      - name: needs_attention
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: True if lifecycle_stage is At Risk or Churned; otherwise false
      - name: is_new_user
        data_type: BOOLEAN
        description: True if lifecycle_stage is New User; otherwise false
      - name: calculated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Timestamp when the query ran; time zone comes from the session

blocks.original_text:
- name: account
      description: Account dimension enriched with visitor counts, NPS aggregates, and all-time usage metrics joined to the latest account profile (one row per account_id)
      grain: One row per account_id
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_pendo__latest_account
      - intermediate.int_pendo__latest_visitor_account
      - intermediate.int_pendo__latest_nps_rating
      - intermediate.int_pendo__account_daily_metrics
      business_logic: '- Use intermediate.int_pendo__latest_account as the base (one record per account_id); all base columns are passed through unchanged. - From intermediate.int_pendo__latest_visitor_account, group by account_id and count unique, non-null visitor_id values to get count_associated_visitors. - From intermediate.int_pendo__latest_nps_rating, group by account_id to compute NPS metrics: minimum rating, maximum rating, and average rating; null ratings are ignored, and if an account has no ratings these fields remain null. - From intermediate.int_pendo__account_daily_metrics, group by account_id and aggregate across all available rows: - count_active_visitors, count_page_viewing_visitors, count_feature_clicking_visitors, sum_minutes, sum_events, count_event_records are summed over time. - count_active_days is the number of unique occurred_on dates (null dates are excluded). - count_active_months is the number of unique calendar months derived from occurred_on (null dates are excluded). - average_daily_minutes is total minutes divided by the number of active days; if there are no active days, this average is 0. - average_daily_events is total events divided by the number of active days; if there are no active days, this average is 0. - first_event_on is the earliest occurred_on date; last_event_on is the latest occurred_on date. - Left join the visitor, NPS, and daily aggregates to the base on account_id. - Default the following metrics to 0 when missing: count_associated_visitors, count_active_visitors, count_page_viewing_visitors, count_feature_clicking_visitors, count_active_days, count_active_months, sum_minutes, sum_events, count_event_records, average_daily_minutes, average_daily_events. NPS metrics and event dates are not defaulted. - The result contains exactly one row per account_id.'
      columns:
      - name: account_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary key from latest_account and join key; one output row per account_id.
      - name: last_updated_at
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pass-through last update timestamp string from latest_account; may be null.
      - name: account_id_hash
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Pass-through numeric hash of account_id from latest_account; may be null.
      - name: first_visit_at
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pass-through first visit timestamp string from latest_account; may be null.
      - name: last_visit_at
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Pass-through last visit timestamp string from latest_account; may be null.
      - name: latest_account_index
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Pass-through ordering/index field from latest_account; may be null.
      - name: count_associated_visitors
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of unique non-null visitors linked to the account; left joined and defaulted to 0 when none.
      - name: min_nps_rating
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Minimum NPS rating for the account; null ratings ignored; remains null if no ratings exist.
      - name: max_nps_rating
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Maximum NPS rating for the account; null ratings ignored; remains null if no ratings exist.
      - name: avg_nps_rating
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average NPS rating for the account; null ratings ignored; unrounded; remains null if no ratings exist.
      - name: count_active_visitors
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of daily active visitor counts across all time for the account; defaulted to 0 when missing.
      - name: count_page_viewing_visitors
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of daily page-viewing visitor counts across all time for the account; defaulted to 0 when missing.
      - name: count_feature_clicking_visitors
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum of daily feature-clicking visitor counts across all time for the account; defaulted to 0 when missing.
      - name: count_active_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of unique occurred_on dates with activity for the account; defaulted to 0 when none.
      - name: count_active_months
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of unique calendar months with activity based on occurred_on; defaulted to 0 when none.
      - name: sum_minutes
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Total minutes of activity summed across all daily records for the account; defaulted to 0 when missing.
      - name: sum_events
        data_type: HUGEINT

specification.name: account
specification.description: Account dimension enriched with visitor counts, NPS aggregates, and all-time usage metrics joined to the latest account profile (one row per account_id)
specification.grain: One row per account_id
specification.business_logic: - Use intermediate.int_pendo__latest_account as the base (one record per account_id); all base columns are passed through unchanged. - From intermediate.int_pendo__latest_visitor_account, group by account_id and count unique, non-null visitor_id values to get count_associated_visitors. - From intermediate.int_pendo__latest_nps_rating, group by account_id to compute NPS metrics: minimum rating, maximum rating, and average rating; null ratings are ignored, and if an account has no ratings these fields remain null. - From intermediate.int_pendo__account_daily_metrics, group by account_id and aggregate across all available rows: - count_active_visitors, count_page_viewing_visitors, count_feature_clicking_visitors, sum_minutes, sum_events, count_event_records are summed over time. - count_active_days is the number of unique occurred_on dates (null dates are excluded). - count_active_months is the number of unique calendar months derived from occurred_on (null dates are excluded). - average_daily_minutes is total minutes divided by the number of active days; if there are no active days, this average is 0. - average_daily_events is total events divided by the number of active days; if there are no active days, this average is 0. - first_event_on is the earliest occurred_on date; last_event_on is the latest occurred_on date. - Left join the visitor, NPS, and daily aggregates to the base on account_id. - Default the following metrics to 0 when missing: count_associated_visitors, count_active_visitors, count_page_viewing_visitors, count_feature_clicking_visitors, count_active_days, count_active_months, sum_minutes, sum_events, count_event_records, average_daily_minutes, average_daily_events. NPS metrics and event dates are not defaulted. - The result contains exactly one row per account_id.

- name: account_daily_metrics
      description: Daily account-level metrics aligned to a calendar spine from each account's first event through the current date.
      grain: One row per account_id per date_day; rows may duplicate if the source has multiple records for the same (account_id, occurred_on).
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_pendo__calendar_spine
      - intermediate.int_pendo__account_daily_metrics
      business_logic: '- Reference all calendar dates (date_day) from intermediate.int_pendo__calendar_spine. - Reference daily account metrics from intermediate.int_pendo__account_daily_metrics. - For each account_id present in daily_metrics, compute first_event_on as the minimum occurred_on. - Build an account-specific calendar by pairing each account_id with every date_day such that: - date_day >= first_event_on - date_day <= the current date at execution time (cast(current_timestamp as date), using warehouse/system timezone). - Left join this account-specific calendar to daily_metrics on: - account_id equality - date_day equals occurred_on - Copy metric columns directly from daily_metrics; when no match exists for a given (account_id, date_day), all metric columns are NULL. - No aggregation, de-duplication, or ordering is applied. If daily_metrics contains multiple rows for the same (account_id, occurred_on), the output includes one row per matching source record (duplicating the calendar row). - Accounts with no rows in daily_metrics do not appear in the output.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: customer_lifecycle_insights
      description: Customer lifecycle insights combining visitor activity, lifecycle segmentation, RFM, product health, and derived journey classifications and scores
      grain: One row per visitor_id (from marts.pendo__visitor)
      source_models:
      - marts.pendo__visitor
      - intermediate.int_pendo__user_lifecycle_segments
      - intermediate.int_pendo__customer_rfm_analysis
      - intermediate.int_pendo__product_health_metrics
      business_logic: 'Build a comprehensive customer record per visitor_id by joining base visitor activity with lifecycle, RFM, and product health, then derive journey labels, values, and recommendations: 1) Base rowset and joins - Start from marts.pendo__visitor (vb), one row per visitor_id; carry: visitor_id, account_id, first_event_on, last_event_on, count_active_days, count_active_months, sum_events, sum_minutes, average_daily_events, average_daily_minutes, count_associated_accounts. - Left join intermediate.int_pendo__user_lifecycle_segments (lc) on visitor_id. - Left join intermediate.int_pendo__customer_rfm_analysis (rfm) on visitor_id. - Left join intermediate.int_pendo__product_health_metrics (ph) on account_id. - Null policy: Left joins may yield missing lifecycle/RFM/health attributes; unless explicitly defaulted in rules below, missing values do not match conditions and fall to the default outcome. 2) Customer segmentation label (customer_segment_label) evaluated in order: - Power User + Champions → "Star Customer" - (Mature User or Power User) + High Value → "Key Account" - New User + New Customers → "Fresh Prospect" - Growing User + Potential Loyalists → "Rising Star" - churn_risk_level in (High Risk, Medium Risk) + At Risk → "Save Immediately" - lifecycle_stage = At Risk + action_priority = Re-engagement → "Rescue Mission" - lifecycle_stage = Churned → "Lost Customer" - Else → "Standard Customer" 3) Comprehensive customer value (comprehensive_customer_value, 0–100): - Compute a weighted sum: 40% of user_value_score (defaults to 0 if missing), 30% of (rfm_composite_score scaled to 0–100 by multiplying by 20; defaults to 0 if missing), and 30% of overall_health_score (defaults to 50 if missing). Cap the result at 100. No rounding beyond native numeric evaluation. 4) Recommended next action (recommended_next_action) evaluated in order: - Power User + Champions → "Leverage as advocate; Offer exclusive features; Request testimonials" - is_new_user = true + New Customers → "Intensive onboarding; Feature education; Success manager assignment" - needs_attention = true + action_priority = Re-engagement → "Personalized outreach; Usage analysis; Feature recommendations" - churn_risk_level = High Risk → "Immediate intervention; Executive outreach; Value demonstration" - lifecycle_stage = Growing User → "Feature adoption campaign; Usage optimization; Upgrade path guidance" - rfm_segment = Loyal Customers → "Upsell opportunities; Loyalty rewards; Advanced feature training" - Else → "Standard nurturing; Regular check-ins; Content engagement" 5) Customer journey stage (customer_journey_stage): - Define days since first event as the number of days from the first_event_on date to today. - If days since first event ≤ 30 → "Onboarding" - Else if lifecycle_stage in (Growing User, Mature User) and customer_value_tier in (High Value, Medium Value) → "Growth" - Else if lifecycle_stage in (Power User, Mature User) and rfm_segment in (Champions, Loyal Customers) → "Maturity" - Else if churn_risk_level in (High Risk, Medium Risk) or lifecycle_stage = At Risk → "Retention" - Else if lifecycle_stage = Churned → "Win-back" - Else → "Maintenance" 6) Predicted LTV tier (predicted_ltv_tier) evaluated in order: - lifecycle_stage in (Power User, Mature User) + customer_value_tier = High Value + overall_health_score ≥ 70 (treat missing health as 60 for this rule) → "Very High LTV" - (user_value_score ≥ 70 or rfm_composite_score ≥ 4) + churn_risk_level = Low Risk → "High LTV" - lifecycle_stage in (Growing User, New User) + predicted_clv_tier in (High CLV, Medium CLV) → "Moderate LTV" - churn_risk_level = High Risk or lifecycle_stage = Churned → "Low LTV" - Else → "Standard LTV" 7) Engagement velocity and trends (from comprehensive view): - engagement_velocity: ratio of count_active_days to days since first event; if either value is not positive, set to 0. - usage_trend: define a baseline average as sum_events divided by count_active_days when count_active_days > 0; if average_daily_events exceeds the baseline by more than 20% → "Accelerating"; if within ±20% → "Stable"; otherwise → "Declining". When count_active_days = 0, the baseline is undefined and the outcome is "Declining". - account_influence_level: count_associated_accounts > 3 → "Multi-Account Influencer"; > 1 → "Cross-Account User"; else → "Single Account User". - calculated_at: timestamp when the metrics are computed. 8) Final importance and investment expectation: - customer_importance_level (in order): - customer_segment_label in (Star Customer, Key Account) + predicted_ltv_tier = Very High LTV → "Critical" - comprehensive_customer_value ≥ 80 + customer_journey_stage in (Growth, Maturity) → "High" - comprehensive_customer_value ≥ 60 or customer_segment_label in (Rising Star, Fresh Prospect) → "Medium" - needs_attention = true or customer_journey_stage = Retention → "At Risk" - Else → "Standard" - investment_expectation: - Star Customer → "High ROI - Advocacy & Expansion" - Key Account → "High ROI - Retention & Upsell" - Rising Star → "Medium ROI - Growth Investment" - Fresh Prospect → "Medium ROI - Onboarding Investment" - Save Immediately → "Low ROI - Retention Cost" - Lost Customer → "Negative ROI - Win-back Cost" - Else → "Standard ROI - Maintenance" 9) Output all selected and derived columns; no additional filtering; grain remains one row per visitor_id.'
      columns:
      - name: visitor_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique visitor identifier and grouping key; exactly one output row per visitor_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: account_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Account identifier from the visitor base used to join product health metrics
      - name: first_event_on
        data_type: DATE
        description: Date of the visitor's first recorded event used to compute days since first event
      - name: last_event_on
        data_type: DATE
        description: Date of the visitor's most recent recorded event as carried from the visitor base
      - name: count_active_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of distinct active days for the visitor as carried from the visitor base
      - name: count_active_months
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of distinct active months for the visitor as carried from the visitor base
      - name: sum_events
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total count of events for the visitor; used to form the baseline average as sum_events divided by count_active_days
      - name: sum_minutes
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total minutes of activity for the visitor as carried from the visitor base
      - name: average_daily_events
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average events per calendar day from the visitor base compared against the baseline for usage_trend

specification.name: customer_lifecycle_insights
specification.description: Customer lifecycle insights combining visitor activity, lifecycle segmentation, RFM, product health, and derived journey classifications and scores
specification.grain: One row per visitor_id (from marts.pendo__visitor)
specification.business_logic: Build a comprehensive customer record per visitor_id by joining base visitor activity with lifecycle, RFM, and product health, then derive journey labels, values, and recommendations: 1) Base rowset and joins - Start from marts.pendo__visitor (vb), one row per visitor_id; carry: visitor_id, account_id, first_event_on, last_event_on, count_active_days, count_active_months, sum_events, sum_minutes, average_daily_events, average_daily_minutes, count_associated_accounts. - Left join intermediate.int_pendo__user_lifecycle_segments (lc) on visitor_id. - Left join intermediate.int_pendo__customer_rfm_analysis (rfm) on visitor_id. - Left join intermediate.int_pendo__product_health_metrics (ph) on account_id. - Null policy: Left joins may yield missing lifecycle/RFM/health attributes; unless explicitly defaulted in rules below, missing values do not match conditions and fall to the default outcome. 2) Customer segmentation label (customer_segment_label) evaluated in order: - Power User + Champions → "Star Customer" - (Mature User or Power User) + High Value → "Key Account" - New User + New Customers → "Fresh Prospect" - Growing User + Potential Loyalists → "Rising Star" - churn_risk_level in (High Risk, Medium Risk) + At Risk → "Save Immediately" - lifecycle_stage = At Risk + action_priority = Re-engagement → "Rescue Mission" - lifecycle_stage = Churned → "Lost Customer" - Else → "Standard Customer" 3) Comprehensive customer value (comprehensive_customer_value, 0–100): - Compute a weighted sum: 40% of user_value_score (defaults to 0 if missing), 30% of (rfm_composite_score scaled to 0–100 by multiplying by 20; defaults to 0 if missing), and 30% of overall_health_score (defaults to 50 if missing). Cap the result at 100. No rounding beyond native numeric evaluation. 4) Recommended next action (recommended_next_action) evaluated in order: - Power User + Champions → "Leverage as advocate; Offer exclusive features; Request testimonials" - is_new_user = true + New Customers → "Intensive onboarding; Feature education; Success manager assignment" - needs_attention = true + action_priority = Re-engagement → "Personalized outreach; Usage analysis; Feature recommendations" - churn_risk_level = High Risk → "Immediate intervention; Executive outreach; Value demonstration" - lifecycle_stage = Growing User → "Feature adoption campaign; Usage optimization; Upgrade path guidance" - rfm_segment = Loyal Customers → "Upsell opportunities; Loyalty rewards; Advanced feature training" - Else → "Standard nurturing; Regular check-ins; Content engagement" 5) Customer journey stage (customer_journey_stage): - Define days since first event as the number of days from the first_event_on date to today. - If days since first event ≤ 30 → "Onboarding" - Else if lifecycle_stage in (Growing User, Mature User) and customer_value_tier in (High Value, Medium Value) → "Growth" - Else if lifecycle_stage in (Power User, Mature User) and rfm_segment in (Champions, Loyal Customers) → "Maturity" - Else if churn_risk_level in (High Risk, Medium Risk) or lifecycle_stage = At Risk → "Retention" - Else if lifecycle_stage = Churned → "Win-back" - Else → "Maintenance" 6) Predicted LTV tier (predicted_ltv_tier) evaluated in order: - lifecycle_stage in (Power User, Mature User) + customer_value_tier = High Value + overall_health_score ≥ 70 (treat missing health as 60 for this rule) → "Very High LTV" - (user_value_score ≥ 70 or rfm_composite_score ≥ 4) + churn_risk_level = Low Risk → "High LTV" - lifecycle_stage in (Growing User, New User) + predicted_clv_tier in (High CLV, Medium CLV) → "Moderate LTV" - churn_risk_level = High Risk or lifecycle_stage = Churned → "Low LTV" - Else → "Standard LTV" 7) Engagement velocity and trends (from comprehensive view): - engagement_velocity: ratio of count_active_days to days since first event; if either value is not positive, set to 0. - usage_trend: define a baseline average as sum_events divided by count_active_days when count_active_days > 0; if average_daily_events exceeds the baseline by more than 20% → "Accelerating"; if within ±20% → "Stable"; otherwise → "Declining". When count_active_days = 0, the baseline is undefined and the outcome is "Declining". - account_influence_level: count_associated_accounts > 3 → "Multi-Account Influencer"; > 1 → "Cross-Account User"; else → "Single Account User". - calculated_at: timestamp when the metrics are computed. 8) Final importance and investment expectation: - customer_importance_level (in order): - customer_segment_label in (Star Customer, Key Account) + predicted_ltv_tier = Very High LTV → "Critical" - comprehensive_customer_value ≥ 80 + customer_journey_stage in (Growth, Maturity) → "High" - comprehensive_customer_value ≥ 60 or customer_segment_label in (Rising Star, Fresh Prospect) → "Medium" - needs_attention = true or customer_journey_stage = Retention → "At Risk" - Else → "Standard" - investment_expectation: - Star Customer → "High ROI - Advocacy & Expansion" - Key Account → "High ROI - Retention & Upsell" - Rising Star → "Medium ROI - Growth Investment" - Fresh Prospect → "Medium ROI - Onboarding Investment" - Save Immediately → "Low ROI - Retention Cost" - Lost Customer → "Negative ROI - Win-back Cost" - Else → "Standard ROI - Maintenance" 9) Output all selected and derived columns; no additional filtering; grain remains one row per visitor_id.

blocks.original_text:
- name: executive_dashboard_metrics
      description: Executive KPI snapshot derived from account history, product health metrics, and 30-day event trends (single-row platform summary)
      grain: Exactly one row (global platform snapshot at execution time)
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_pendo__account_history
      - intermediate.int_pendo__product_health_metrics
      - staging.stg_pendo__event
      business_logic: '- Build account_performance_summary: - Source: staging.stg_pendo__account_history left join intermediate.int_pendo__product_health_metrics on account_id. - One row per account with: account_id, account_name set equal to account_id, agent_is_paying=true, agent_planlevel=''Standard'', first_visit=first_visit_at, last_visit=last_visit_at. - Set per-account defaults: critical_customers=0, high_value_customers=0, customers_at_risk=0, onboarding_customers=0, total_active_users=0, avg_customer_value_score=50.0, high_ltv_customers=0. - For each account, derive product metrics as the maximum values across joined product_health rows: product_health_score (overall_health_score), account_nps (net_promoter_score), feature_adoption_rate, and customer_retention_30d. - Derive revenue_health_indicators from account_performance_summary: - revenue_health_status: - If agent_is_paying and avg_customer_value_score ≥ 80 → Excellent; if agent_is_paying and ≥ 60 → Good; if agent_is_paying and < 60 → At Risk. - If not paying and high_ltv_customers > 0 → Conversion Opportunity; otherwise Standard. - account_risk_level (in order): if customers_at_risk / total_active_users > 0.3 → High Risk; else if > 0.15 → Medium Risk; else if product_health_score < 50 → Medium Risk; else if account_nps < 0 → High Risk; otherwise Low Risk. When total_active_users=0, the ratio is treated as NULL and later rules apply. - growth_potential (in order): if high_ltv_customers > (critical_customers + high_value_customers) and feature_adoption_rate > 0.4 → High Growth Potential; else if onboarding_customers > 0 and avg_customer_value_score > 60 → Moderate Growth Potential; else if total_active_users > 10 and customer_retention_30d > 0.7 → Stable Growth; otherwise Limited Growth. - Aggregate platform_wide_kpis across all accounts in revenue_health_indicators: - total_accounts = distinct account count; paying_accounts = distinct account count where agent_is_paying; conversion_rate = paying_accounts / total_accounts (no zero-denominator guard). - platform_total_users = sum(total_active_users); strategic_customers = sum(critical_customers + high_value_customers); customers_needing_attention = sum(customers_at_risk); new_customers_onboarding = sum(onboarding_customers). Sums ignore NULL inputs. - Averages (NULLs ignored): avg_platform_health_score, avg_platform_nps, avg_feature_adoption, avg_retention_rate, avg_customer_value. - Risk/growth counts: number of accounts labeled High/Medium/Low Risk; number with High Growth Potential; number with revenue_health_status = Excellent; number with revenue_health_status = Conversion Opportunity. - calculation_date = current_date at execution. - Compute trend_analysis from staging.stg_pendo__event over the last 30 days (occurred_at within 30 days of now): - For each day, compute: daily_active_accounts (distinct accounts), daily_active_users (distinct users), daily_total_events (sum of events), daily_total_minutes (sum of minutes). - Across these 30 days, compute averages of the daily metrics and user_activity_volatility as the standard deviation of daily_active_users. - user_growth_rate_7d = (average daily_active_users in the last 7 days minus average in the prior 7 days) divided by the prior 7-day average; if the denominator is zero or missing this rate is NULL; expose user_growth_rate_7d with NULL replaced by 0. - growth_trend_assessment is based on the unfilled (raw) user_growth_rate_7d: >0.1 Strong Growth; >0.05 Moderate Growth; >-0.05 Stable; >-0.1 Slight Decline; otherwise Concerning Decline (NULL falls to the final category). - Produce executive_summary_scorecard (final output, single row): - Cross join platform_wide_kpis with trend_analysis. - overall_business_health_score: weighted composite capped at 100 using: - 25% product health score; 15% normalized NPS (NPS shifted from [-1,1] to [0,100]); 15% feature adoption rate scaled to 0–100; 15% retention rate scaled to 0–100; 10% conversion rate scaled to 0–100; 20% growth component where baseline is 50 and adjusted upward by 100×growth when positive, or scaled down by multiplying 50 by (1 + growth) when negative; specification.name: executive_dashboard_metrics
specification.description: Executive KPI snapshot derived from account history, product health metrics, and 30-day event trends (single-row platform summary)
specification.grain: Exactly one row (global platform snapshot at execution time)
specification.business_logic: - Build account_performance_summary: - Source: staging.stg_pendo__account_history left join intermediate.int_pendo__product_health_metrics on account_id. - One row per account with: account_id, account_name set equal to account_id, agent_is_paying=true, agent_planlevel='Standard', first_visit=first_visit_at, last_visit=last_visit_at. - Set per-account defaults: critical_customers=0, high_value_customers=0, customers_at_risk=0, onboarding_customers=0, total_active_users=0, avg_customer_value_score=50.0, high_ltv_customers=0. - For each account, derive product metrics as the maximum values across joined product_health rows: product_health_score (overall_health_score), account_nps (net_promoter_score), feature_adoption_rate, and customer_retention_30d. - Derive revenue_health_indicators from account_performance_summary: - revenue_health_status: - If agent_is_paying and avg_customer_value_score ≥ 80 → Excellent; if agent_is_paying and ≥ 60 → Good; if agent_is_paying and < 60 → At Risk. - If not paying and high_ltv_customers > 0 → Conversion Opportunity; otherwise Standard. - account_risk_level (in order): if customers_at_risk / total_active_users > 0.3 → High Risk; else if > 0.15 → Medium Risk; else if product_health_score < 50 → Medium Risk; else if account_nps < 0 → High Risk; otherwise Low Risk. When total_active_users=0, the ratio is treated as NULL and later rules apply. - growth_potential (in order): if high_ltv_customers > (critical_customers + high_value_customers) and feature_adoption_rate > 0.4 → High Growth Potential; else if onboarding_customers > 0 and avg_customer_value_score > 60 → Moderate Growth Potential; else if total_active_users > 10 and customer_retention_30d > 0.7 → Stable Growth; otherwise Limited Growth. - Aggregate platform_wide_kpis across all accounts in revenue_health_indicators: - total_accounts = distinct account count; paying_accounts = distinct account count where agent_is_paying; conversion_rate = paying_accounts / total_accounts (no zero-denominator guard). - platform_total_users = sum(total_active_users); strategic_customers = sum(critical_customers + high_value_customers); customers_needing_attention = sum(customers_at_risk); new_customers_onboarding = sum(onboarding_customers). Sums ignore NULL inputs. - Averages (NULLs ignored): avg_platform_health_score, avg_platform_nps, avg_feature_adoption, avg_retention_rate, avg_customer_value. - Risk/growth counts: number of accounts labeled High/Medium/Low Risk; number with High Growth Potential; number with revenue_health_status = Excellent; number with revenue_health_status = Conversion Opportunity. - calculation_date = current_date at execution. - Compute trend_analysis from staging.stg_pendo__event over the last 30 days (occurred_at within 30 days of now): - For each day, compute: daily_active_accounts (distinct accounts), daily_active_users (distinct users), daily_total_events (sum of events), daily_total_minutes (sum of minutes). - Across these 30 days, compute averages of the daily metrics and user_activity_volatility as the standard deviation of daily_active_users. - user_growth_rate_7d = (average daily_active_users in the last 7 days minus average in the prior 7 days) divided by the prior 7-day average; if the denominator is zero or missing this rate is NULL; expose user_growth_rate_7d with NULL replaced by 0. - growth_trend_assessment is based on the unfilled (raw) user_growth_rate_7d: >0.1 Strong Growth; >0.05 Moderate Growth; >-0.05 Stable; >-0.1 Slight Decline; otherwise Concerning Decline (NULL falls to the final category). - Produce executive_summary_scorecard (final output, single row): - Cross join platform_wide_kpis with trend_analysis. - overall_business_health_score: weighted composite capped at 100 using: - 25% product health score; 15% normalized NPS (NPS shifted from [-1,1] to [0,100]); 15% feature adoption rate scaled to 0–100; 15% retention rate scaled to 0–100; 10% conversion rate scaled to 0–100; 20% growth component where baseline is 50 and adjusted upward by 100×growth when positive, or scaled down by multiplying 50 by (1 + growth) when negative; the growth rate used here is the coalesced value. - primary_alert_status (first match wins): high_risk_accounts > 20% of total_accounts → Account Risk Alert; avg_platform_nps < -0.2 → Customer Satisfaction Alert; user_growth_rate_7d < -0.1 → Growth Decline Alert; avg_retention_rate < 0.6 → Retention Alert; customers_needing_attention > 25% of platform_total_users → Customer Health Alert; otherwise All Systems Normal. - strategic_recommendation (first match wins): conversion_opportunities > 10% of paying_accounts → Focus on conversion optimization; high_growth_accounts > 20% of total_accounts → Capitalize on growth opportunities; customers_needing_attention > strategic_customers → Prioritize customer success initiatives; user_growth_rate_7d < 0 → Address user acquisition and retention; otherwise Maintain current strategy with incremental improvements. - generated_at = current_timestamp at execution.

agent_sql.raw_text: WITH m AS (SELECT feature_id,count(DISTINCT visitor_id) count_visitors,count(DISTINCT account_id) count_accounts,sum(num_events) sum_clicks,count(*) count_click_events,min(occurred_at) first_click_at,max(occurred_at) last_click_at,round(sum(num_minutes)/NULLIF(count(DISTINCT visitor_id),0),3) avg_visitor_minutes,round(sum(num_events)/NULLIF(count(DISTINCT visitor_id),0),3) avg_visitor_events FROM staging.stg_pendo__feature_event GROUP BY 1) SELECT f.*,coalesce(m.count_visitors,0) count_visitors,coalesce(m.count_accounts,0) count_accounts,coalesce(m.sum_clicks,0) sum_clicks,coalesce(m.count_click_events,0) count_click_events,m.first_click_at,m.last_click_at,coalesce(m.avg_visitor_minutes,0) avg_visitor_minutes,coalesce(m.avg_visitor_events,0) avg_visitor_events FROM intermediate.int_pendo__feature_info f LEFT JOIN m USING(feature_id)

- name: feature

      grain: One row per feature_id
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_pendo__feature_info
      - staging.stg_pendo__feature_event

- name: feature_event
      description: Feature interaction events enriched with current and previous feature metadata
      grain: One row per stg_pendo__feature_event record with a matching feature_id in int_pendo__feature_info
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_pendo__feature_event
      - intermediate.int_pendo__feature_info
      - intermediate.int_pendo__latest_account
      - intermediate.int_pendo__latest_visitor
      business_logic: '- Begin with all rows and columns from staging.stg_pendo__feature_event; no filtering, casting, or aggregation. - For each visitor_id, sort events by occurred_at ascending and populate: - previous_feature_id: the feature_id from the immediately prior event for that visitor. - previous_feature_event_at: the occurred_at from the immediately prior event. - previous_feature_num_minutes: the num_minutes from the immediately prior event. - previous_feature_num_events: the num_events from the immediately prior event. If there is no prior event, these fields are NULL. If multiple events share the same occurred_at for a visitor, the chosen prior row follows the database’s default ordering. - Inner join to intermediate.int_pendo__feature_info on the current event’s feature_id to add current feature attributes (feature_name, page_id, page_name, product_area_name, group_id as product_area_id, app_display_name, app_platform). Events without a match are removed. - Left join to intermediate.int_pendo__feature_info on previous_feature_id to add previous feature attributes (previous_feature_name, previous_feature_page_id, previous_feature_page_name, previous_feature_product_area_name, previous_feature_product_area_id). If previous_feature_id is NULL or has no match, these attributes are NULL. - Left join to intermediate.int_pendo__latest_visitor on visitor_id and intermediate.int_pendo__latest_account on account_id; no columns are selected from these joins. Row count is unchanged unless duplicate keys exist in those sources. - Output all source columns, the four previous_* fields, and the selected current and previous feature attributes; no final ordering is applied.'
      columns:
      - name: account_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Source account identifier; used only to support a left join; pass-through; may be NULL
      - name: app_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Source application identifier; pass-through; may be NULL
      - name: feature_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current event feature identifier; required for the inner join to feature_info; events without a match are dropped
      - name: num_events
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Event count for this record; pass-through; may be NULL; no rounding applied
      - name: num_minutes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Elapsed minutes for this record; pass-through; may be NULL; no rounding applied
      - name: remote_ip
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Source remote IP address; pass-through; may be NULL; no normalization applied
      - name: server_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Source server name; pass-through; may be NULL; no normalization applied
      - name: occurred_at
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Event timestamp used to order events within each visitor ascending; ties are not deterministically broken
      - name: user_agent
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Source user agent string; pass-through; may be NULL; casing and whitespace preserved
      - name: visitor_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Visitor identifier that defines the window for previous_* calculations; pass-through; may be NULL
      - name: feature_event_key
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Opaque event key from the source; pass-through; uniqueness not enforced
      - name: previous_feature_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Feature identifier from the immediately prior event for the same visitor when ordered by occurred_at ascending; NULL for the first event or if ordering ties occur
      - name: previous_feature_event_at
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Timestamp from the immediately prior event for the same visitor; NULL for the first event or if ordering ties occur
      - name: previous_feature_num_minutes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: num_minutes from the immediately prior event for the same visitor; NULL for the first event; no rounding applied
      - name: previous_feature_num_events
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: num_events from the immediately prior event for the same visitor; NULL for the first event; no rounding applied
